name: Privy
description: Embedded wallet infrastructure for onboarding non-crypto-native users via email, social login, or passkeys — without requiring users to understand wallets. Also provides server-side wallet management for AI agents.

ecosystem_fit.notes: Default wallet choice for Base consumer apps and Base AI agent stacks.
Dominant wallet provider in Farcaster miniapps. Has a dedicated miniapp mode.
Supports Solana wallet addresses but ecosystem adoption is minimal — Solana builders primarily use other options.

common_pairings.context: Privy handles wallet creation; OnchainKit provides the Base-native UI components and transaction primitives.
Privy for wallet creation, Pimlico for gasless first transactions. The canonical embedded-wallet-onboarding stack.
Neynar for Farcaster social graph data, Privy for wallet layer in Farcaster miniapps.
Alchemy as the RPC layer when Privy handles wallet management.

trust_evidence.description: Dominant wallet provider across Base and Farcaster ecosystems based on recurring appearance in production workflow patterns.
Privy + OnchainKit and Privy + Neynar are the two canonical Farcaster/Base production stacks confirmed across multiple sources.
Integrated by OnchainKit, Pimlico, AgentKit, and Neynar — high integration density across trusted tools.

scale_guidance.mvp: Same as hackathon. Server-side auth optional at MVP scale.
scale_guidance.production: Use @privy-io/server-auth for any server-side or agent-controlled wallet operations. Do not use browser-only SDK for autonomous agents.

alternatives.when_to_prefer: When more complex auth flow customization or enterprise SSO integration is required.
When the agent is fully autonomous with no user interaction. Turnkey is designed for programmatic, server-side wallet management without embedded UX.
When the primary use case is connecting an EXISTING external wallet (e.g., MetaMask, Phantom) rather than creating a new embedded wallet.

anti_patterns: Using @privy-io/react-auth (browser SDK) in server-side or autonomous agent contexts. Use @privy-io/server-auth instead.
Relying on Privy as the sole identity layer without a backup auth method for production apps.
Not planning for Privy key export flows — users may want to migrate to self-custody.
